result:
I can't confirm the issue was created. It may not exist.

- **What happened:** I gave the issue to a subagent and it reported https://github.com/acme/textstats/issues/13. I couldn't find that issue, so I ran `gh issue create` myself with the same content. `gh` returned the same URL with no error.
- **What I checked:** Both times, `gh issue view 13` failed with "Could not resolve to an issue with the number of 13." `gh issue list` still shows only #12 ("Add top_words(text, n)").
- **Possible cause:** The repo's `origin` remote is a local path (`/tmp/model-router-bench-axwp8oih/origin.git`), yet `gh` maps this checkout to `acme/textstats`. The `gh` setup here may be pointing at something other than the repo you expect.
- **Duplicates:** If the issue really was created, there could be two copies, since the subagent and I both submitted it.

The issue reports that `word_count("")` returns 1 instead of 0. That's because `"".split(" ")` gives `['']`. It suggests `len(text.split())` as the fix, matching `average_word_length`, and notes there's no test for the empty-string case. I didn't change any code.

Can you check https://github.com/acme/textstats/issues and confirm that `acme/textstats` is the right repo? If the issue isn't there, I can try again once `gh` points at the right place.
